summary: Targeted retest of the iter-14 HIGH-severity bug in /app/frontend/src/lib/analytics.js:59. Spread order fix (from `{...properties, ...attr, variant}` to `{...attr, ...properties, variant}`) verified working: caller-supplied `source` now wins over attribution, and attribution still fills in as fallback when caller does not supply source.

tests_executed.description: Anonymous visitor lands with utm_source=linkedin (attribution.source=linkedin). Click [data-testid='nav-signin-btn']. Verify POST /api/analytics/track properties.source === 'top_nav'.
Same session with attribution.source=linkedin. Click [data-testid='nav-waitlist-btn']. Verify POST properties.source === 'top_nav'.
page_view is emitted without caller-supplied source. Verify properties.source falls back to attribution ('linkedin' due to utm_source=linkedin).
tests_executed.notes: Confirms attribution logic was NOT broken by the swap - caller-absent still gets attribution.
/dashboard correctly redirects anonymous user to '/' (root landing). /login triggers window.location.href to auth.emergentagent.com (intercepted by Playwright abort as expected).

tests_executed.description: Verify [data-testid='waitlist-email'] and [data-testid='waitlist-submit'] still present on landing.

console_errors.details: All 10 are HTTP 401 responses from /api/auth/me — expected behavior for anonymous visitors; not related to bug fix.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and minimal. Note: the change means that if a caller intentionally passes {source: null/undefined} it will now leak `null` and override attribution — but current call sites (Layout.jsx track('signin_click',{source:'top_nav'}) and track('waitlist_button_click',{source:'top_nav'})) always pass non-null strings, so this is safe. If future callers pass explicit null, consider a guard: `properties: { ...attr, ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(properties).filter(([_,v])=>v!==null&&v!==undefined)), variant }`.

Minor: page_view event fires only from landing/other pages; attribution keys (medium, campaign, referrer_host) are correctly preserved from attribution when caller only specifies `source`. This means callers overriding source no longer lose the medium/campaign context — verified in captured payloads (medium='social' preserved alongside source='top_nav').
test_credentials: Not used — all tests were anonymous. Admin session_token=test_admin_1784712404860 was available but not needed.
seed_data_creation: None — cleared localStorage before test to ensure fresh attribution capture from utm_source=linkedin.

Caller-supplied `source` now takes precedence in track() payload while attribution still fills in for callers that omit source. All 5 targeted checks passed with zero non-expected console errors.
